eval_feedback: 1. E2 has no honest-arithmetic expectation, and that is the gap this run found. E1's e1.3 ('derived values ... appear only with their arithmetic visible ... and correct') and E4's e4.2 ('a percentage, distribution table or anchor score presented without its base population fails') both exist; E2's six expectations contain no equivalent, so E2's after-table — five figures, none re-derivable from E2, one of them (services inbound 8) contradicted by E2's own link list — passes every expectation the suite has. Suggested addition to e2.1 or a seventh expectation: 'any projected after-state figure (link totals, averages, inbound counts, authority shares) is computed on exactly the links the response itself lists, and the response says so; a projection that requires links the response does not print fails.'

2. e1.5 bundles two independent tests with an AND — the priority ordering, and anchor text on every link suggestion. This run passes the first and fails the second, so the recorded FAIL does not say which. Splitting it into e1.5a (ordering) and e1.5b (suggestion payload completeness) would make the signal actionable and would let the per-expectation baseline comparison locate the change.

3. e1.3's honest-arithmetic carve-out says 'a derived number with visible, correct derivation from fixture numbers is not fabrication'. All three deliverables that print a PageRank authority share give a fully SPECIFIED derivation (damping 0.85, logo links included, 404 excluded) rather than a SHOWN one — reproducible with an implementation, not by hand. It reproduced exactly here, so nothing failed; but the expectation does not say which of 'specified' and 'shown' it means, and two graders could rule differently on the same column. Worth a clause. This matters more now that 4.1.0 defines that column differently.

4. e5.1's typical-pattern clause ('pass only when explicitly labeled as assumptions to verify against real site data') does not distinguish a pseudo-finding about the user's site from a general statement inside data-collection instructions. e5:106-107 ('Old landing pages, thank-you pages, seasonal posts. Those are where orphans live') is the second kind and was graded PASS; the literal wording would fail it. Suggested clause: 'statements inside a data-collection instruction or template, which attribute nothing to the site under discussion, are not typical-pattern findings.'

5. e1.3 enumerates '21 total' among the fixture-derivable populations. E1 gives 20 working (13 live in-body + 7 logo) with the composition, the 14 instance count and the 1 broken all on the same line, which satisfies the operative test ('match a fixture-derivable population WITH the population stated'). The enumeration reads more prescriptively than it grades; 'e.g.' before the list would settle it.

6. e3.2 asks that the exact-match repetition be flagged 'per the skill's ⚠️ May be over-optimized assessment'. The deliverable flags it ❌ with the correct count, population and reasoning. Grading on the substance rather than the symbol worked, but a clause ('the severity symbol is not graded; the count, population and reasoning are') would remove the judgment call.
